item.title: Kotohiragu Autumn Festival — Guide
item.description: The Kotohiragu Autumn Festival is the great annual celebration of Konpira-san, the beloved shrine above Kotohira, held over several days in October. Its highlight is a solemn and stately procession in which a portable shrine (mikoshi) carrying the deity is borne down the shrine’s famous long stone stairway and through the town, accompanied by priests, attendants in traditional costume, and ceremonial regalia — a dignified spectacle rooted in centuries of tradition.

item.title: Nagasaki Kunchi Festival — Guide
item.description: Nagasaki Kunchi, held every year from 7–9 October, is the grand autumn festival of Suwa Shrine and one of Japan’s most spectacular and internationally flavoured festivals, listed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. Dating back nearly 400 years, it showcases the city’s unique cosmopolitan culture through dazzling performances (hono-odori) presented by the city’s neighbourhoods, which take turns each year. The most famous is the electrifying Dragon Dance (Ja Odori), of Chinese origin, in which a long serpentine dragon chases a golden ball to pounding drums, but the festival also features spectacular spinning floats — dashi and elaborate boat- and whale-shaped floats hauled and spun by teams — reflecting Dutch, Chinese and Japanese influences.

item.title: Ohara Festival — Guide
item.description: The Ohara Festival (Ohara Matsuri) is Kagoshima city’s largest and liveliest festival, held every year in early November. Its centrepiece is a huge mass street dance in which around 20,000 participants — organised into teams from companies, schools and community groups, dressed in matching happi coats, yukata and colourful costumes — dance together down the city’s main streets to the infectious rhythm of local folk songs, above all the famous ‘Ohara-bushi’.

item.title: Yamanashi Wine Festival: Tasting the Harvest in Japan's Wine Country — Guide
item.description: Yamanashi’s wine festivals are held in autumn around the grape harvest, gathering local wineries together for open-air tasting events that let visitors sample dozens of regional wines in a single place, often for a set entry fee that includes a tasting glass. Centred on the Katsunuma and Kofu wine districts, these festivals celebrate the region’s identity as the birthplace of Japanese wine, combining tastings with food stalls, local produce and a festive harvest-season atmosphere among the golden vineyards.

item.title: Ikaho Onsen: A Historic Stone-Step Hot Spring Town — Guide
item.description: Ikaho Onsen’s most distinctive feature is its main street — a flight of 365 stone steps, one for each day of the year, lined with ryokan, shops and shrines climbing up the hillside, said to represent life’s journey. The town’s hot spring water, tinged a striking rust-orange from its high iron content and known as ‘golden water’ (kogane no yu), contrasts with the clear ‘silver water’ (shirogane no yu) also found here, and each September the town celebrates its heritage with a lively Stone Steps Festival featuring traditional performances along the steps.
